title: Digitising the Spaza: Hybrid Cash–Digital Payment Practices and Selective Formalisation Among Township Spaza Shops in Tlhabane, Rustenburg, South Africa
content: Spaza shops are central to food access and livelihoods in South African townships, yet little is known about how they combine digital payments with persistent cash use and partial formalisation. This convergent mixed-methods study surveyed a stratified random sample of 150 spaza owners in Tlhabane Township, Rustenburg, and conducted 19 semi-structured interviews with owners and key informants. Immigrant entrepreneurs owned 86.7% of shops. Respondents reported 2.25 payment device or platform mentions per shop, led by Flash (63.3%) and Yoco (54.0%), yet 95.9% preferred cash, 87.8% received most sales in cash, and 76.3% of employers paid wages in cash. Customer preference (96.0%) and convenience (95.3%) dominated reasons for cash use, and 50.7% also cited tax avoidance. Interviews suggested that owners use vending platforms and card terminals for different purposes, and that cash-only supplier deliveries and slow card settlement keep cash floats essential. Registration was selective: 91.3% were registered with municipal or provincial authorities and 78.7% with protection associations, but only 10.7% each with the tax authority and the companies registry. The findings reveal a hybrid cash–digital ‘dual operational reality’ and selective formalisation. Digitalisation policy should combine supplier-side instant payments, simplified tax and transparent engagement with associational governance.
